To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dynamic equilibrium price for oil is a function of three variables: 1) the cost of production of the marginal producer; 2) the cost of the marginal producer’s opportunity cost of capital; 3) the political preferences of the marginal producer.
the equilibrium price range of a mineral commodity is defined by a combination of economic factors and political constraints.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the articulation between the economic and political factors that determine the equilibrium price of oil.
the following questions: What are the economic factors which determine oil prices?
the articulation between economics, politics and uncertainty.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oil market has a dynamic equilibrium price range.
the political factors have been and will continue to be the dominant influence in the formation of the equilibrium price range of crude oil.
the oil price is determined by the interaction of political factors and the dynamic economic equilibrium price range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the economic analysis of oil prices can be extended to take account of the political factors that have been so important in the recent history of oil prices.
the political factors are the main factors in the determination of the oil price range and economic factors are the main determinants in the determination of oil price within the price range.
the dynamic equilibrium price range is a function of the economic and political factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the oil price range is determined by economic factors, but that the equilibrium price range is determined both by economic factors (the cost of extraction and the cost of alternative sources of energy) and by political preferences.
the oil market is not an efficient market, and it is not possible to determine a dynamic equilibrium price of oil.

there is a need for a new oil producer–consumer dialogue, but that the dialogue must take place within the context of an understanding of what the equilibrium price range of a mineral commodity is and what it is not.
